comparison.title: Plan comparison
comparison.subtitle: Every plan includes the full platform. Tiers differ by usage capacity.

1.a: Plans are based on active retail connections: buyers in your Clients module that have placed at least one order in the last 90 days. Your tier is applied from that count on each billing date.

2.a: Yes. Every new distributor gets a 30-day free trial with full Dashboard access. Billing starts on day 31 if you continue.

3.q: What are the benefits of annual billing?
3.a: Annual billing is priced at 10× the monthly rate (2 months free), about 17% savings versus paying month to month.

4.q: What payment methods do you accept?
4.a: We accept bank transfer (BCA, Mandiri, BRI), virtual accounts, and credit/debit cards.

5.q: Can I upgrade or downgrade my plan?
5.a: Yes. As your active retail connections grow, you can move to a higher tier. Downgrades take effect at the next billing cycle.

6.q: Do all plans include Marketplace and Driver?
6.a: Yes. Every plan includes the full Laku loop (Dashboard, Marketplace buyer app, and Driver) with no feature gating by tier. Plans only differ by usage capacity (products, agents, drivers, orders, and similar limits).

7.a: Enterprise is for distributors with 10,000+ active retailers who need custom pricing, SLA, and onboarding support. Contact sales for a quote.

8.q: What happens if I reach a usage limit?
8.a: We use soft caps during MVP: you get a warning around 80% of a quota and an upgrade nudge if you go over. We do not hard-block mid-cycle yet. Optional hard caps (for example new product publishes) may be added later.

hero.title: Our Story: Why We Built Laku
hero.subtitle: Empowering Indonesia’s distributors and retailers with technology that truly works for them.

story.1: For as long as I can remember, trade has been the lifeblood of local communities. In Indonesia, thousands of distributors, warungs, small shops, and independent retailers play a vital role in keeping daily essentials accessible and affordable. Yet, behind this vibrant economy lies a reality that few outsiders see: the struggle of sales, inventory, and orders in a world that is still largely offline, manual, and fragmented.
story.2: As I observed how distribution and retail worked, I noticed the same patterns everywhere. Distributors had to juggle spreadsheets for their product listings, rely on countless WhatsApp messages for order-taking, make endless phone calls to confirm payments, and keep manual notes to track stock. Scheduling shipments was a puzzle in itself: no single system could give them clarity over what was coming in, what was going out, and when. This constant switching between disconnected tools created bottlenecks, wasted time, and left plenty of room for costly mistakes.
story.3: On the other side of the trade, small retailers (the warungs, kiosks, and mom-and-pop shops that form the backbone of our communities) faced equally daunting challenges. For many of them, securing reliable supply was not easy. They often depended on local distributors or middlemen, leaving them with limited access to product variety and fluctuating prices. They lacked visibility into shipments, and often didn’t know if their orders would arrive on time. For businesses running on tight margins, even the smallest disruption meant lost sales and disappointed customers.
story.4: Another challenge I saw was in the way sales happened on the ground. Distributors’ salespeople often had to physically visit retail shops, waiting their turn among a line of other salesmen from different brands or suppliers. This meant that shop owners and buyers were bombarded with product pitches in quick succession, leading to information overload and decision fatigue. Many times, salesmen would have to leave the shop before even getting a chance to present, simply because the buyer was overwhelmed or out of time. This not only wasted effort, but also meant that great products and deals could be missed entirely.
story.5: It became clear to me that the problem wasn’t with the people, but with the system. Sales, inventory, and logistics were happening in silos. There was no single platform to bring order to the chaos. And because of this gap, growth was harder than it needed to be. Distributors couldn’t scale efficiently, and retailers couldn’t compete fairly.
story.6: I didn’t set out to build just another B2B marketplace. Instead, I wanted to reimagine how distribution and retail could work if technology truly empowered both sides. Laku was designed as more than a place to transact. It is a platform where distributors can sell smarter, manage their stock in real-time, schedule and track shipments, and analyze performance, all in one place. At the same time, it gives retailers a simpler, more reliable way to discover products, place orders, and restock with confidence.
story.7: The name Laku itself reflects this spirit. In Indonesian, “laku” means both sale and movement. Trade is all about movement: of goods, of opportunities, of livelihoods. Our platform exists to ensure that this movement happens seamlessly, transparently, and with trust.
story.8: What drives me most is the belief that technology should make life easier, not more complicated. Laku is about bringing modern tools (automation, real-time visibility, and smart data) into a space that has long been underserved. It’s about giving distributors back the time and clarity they need to focus on growth. It’s about giving retailers the access and reliability they deserve to serve their customers better.
story.9: Every feature in Laku comes from this simple vision: to integrate what was once scattered, and to simplify what was once complicated.
story.10: This is not just about building software. It’s about building trust, efficiency, and opportunity for millions of businesses who keep our economy moving every day.
story.vision: That realization sparked the vision for Laku.
story.mission: We are just at the beginning of this journey, but the mission is clear. Trade in Indonesia, and beyond, deserves a platform built for its unique challenges: one that empowers both sellers and buyers equally. With Laku, I believe we can create an ecosystem where distribution thrives, retailers grow, and communities benefit.
story.end: And this is just the start.

1.title: Our Mission
1.content: To empower businesses of every size, from large distributors to small warungs and kiosks, by giving them tools to trade smarter, faster, and more profitably.

2.title: Our Vision
2.content: A future where every retailer in Indonesia, no matter how small, has equal access to products, prices, and opportunities, and every distributor can reach new markets effortlessly.

terms.content:
These Terms & Conditions (“Terms”) govern your access to and use of the Laku Service.

Laku is a B2B e-commerce infrastructure platform built to modernize, facilitate, and fuel Indonesia’s FMCG distribution ecosystem. It combines a vertical SaaS platform for distributors with a marketplace for their buyers (small shops, kiosks, warungs, and local retailers), designed to streamline operations, protect sensitive pricing information, and create a trusted environment for both parties to transact.

By creating an Account or using the Laku Service, you agree to these Terms and the Privacy Policy. If you use Laku for a company, you confirm you are authorized to bind that company.

If you do not agree, do not use the Laku Service.

---

## 1. Definitions

**1.1 “Laku” / “We”** means the operator of the Laku Service.

**1.2 “Laku Service”** means Laku websites, Distributor Dashboard, Buyer Marketplace (mobile and web), Driver application, APIs, and related features we provide from time to time.

**1.3 “Account”** means your registered user profile used to access the Laku Service.

**1.4 “User” / “You”** means a distributor, buyer, driver, staff member, or other person or entity using the Laku Service.

**1.5 “Distributor Dashboard”** means the SaaS tools for distributors, including menus such as Home (Dashboard), Clients (Buyers and Suppliers), Products, Orders, Offers (programs and incentives), Marketing (Team and Campaigns), Analytics (Financial, Sales, and Operational), Automation, Marketplace, Logistics, and Settings.

**1.6 “Marketplace”** means the buyer-facing ordering environment for verified retailers.

**1.7 “Applicable Law”** means the laws and regulations of the Republic of Indonesia.

**1.8 “Personal Data”** has the meaning in the Privacy Policy.

---

## 2. Eligibility and Account registration

**2.1** You must be at least 17 years old and legally competent under Applicable Law. If you are not competent, a guardian or legal representative must supervise and remain responsible.

**2.2** Depending on the product surface, registration may require information such as name, email, phone number, username, password, store or company name, and business details. Distributor Dashboard users may sign in with Google where that option is enabled. Marketplace users may verify phone numbers by OTP (SMS or WhatsApp).

**2.3** We may reject, delay, or require re-verification of registration if information is incomplete, inaccurate, or not permitted under Applicable Law. We are not obliged to state a reason where law allows.

**2.4** You must keep Account credentials and OTP codes confidential. You are responsible for activity under your Account. Notify us promptly of suspected unauthorized access.

**2.5** We may require business verification. This may include Business Registration Number / **NIB**, **NPWP** / Tax ID, company deed or operational permits, bank account details for settlements, and related compliance checks (including document and business-license verification status). Failure to complete verification may limit features or lead to suspension.

---

## 3. Roles and permitted use

**3.1 Distributors** may manage their own catalog, stock, prices, clients, orders, offers, marketing tools, analytics, logistics, marketplace publishing, automations, and settings within their Account. Distributors must not access another distributor’s confidential data.

**3.2 Buyers** may browse and order from distributors according to Marketplace rules, track orders, submit payment proofs where required, and use reviews or returns features as provided.

**3.3 Drivers** may access assigned deliveries, update status, submit proof of delivery or failure evidence, and share location while performing delivery work through the Driver app.

**3.4** You must use the Laku Service only for lawful wholesale and retail distribution purposes.

---

## 4. Pricing confidentiality and fair competition

**4.1** A core purpose of Laku is to protect distributor pricing and reduce harmful price wars. Platform design may restrict cross-distributor price comparison and competitor data access.

**4.2** You must not scrape, harvest, reverse engineer, or bypass controls to obtain another party’s confidential prices, customer lists, or analytics.

**4.3** Breach of this Section is a material breach and may result in immediate suspension.

---

## 5. Orders, payments, delivery, and returns

**5.1** Laku provides technology for Users to create and manage transactions. Unless a separate written agreement says otherwise, **Laku is not the seller of goods**. The sales contract for goods is between buyer and distributor.

**5.2** Distributors are responsible for product legality, quality, labeling, stock accuracy, pricing they set, and fulfilment commitments.

**5.3** Buyers are responsible for accurate order and delivery information and for paying according to the payment method and terms shown for the order (including manual bank transfer and upload of payment proof where applicable).

**5.4** Payment confirmation, cancellations, returns, and logistics status follow the workflows in the Laku Service. Distributors may need to verify payment proofs before marking an order paid.

**5.5** Drivers and distributors must submit accurate delivery or failure documentation. Misrepresentation of delivery status is prohibited.

---

## 6. Fees

**6.1** Use of Laku may be subject to SaaS subscription fees, transaction commissions, and fees for optional services, as published on Laku pricing pages or in a written order form / invoice.

**6.2** Fees and taxes (including VAT where applicable) will be stated in IDR unless otherwise agreed in writing.

**6.3** We may change fees with prior notice through the Laku Service or email. Continued use after the effective date constitutes acceptance, subject to any mandatory rights under Applicable Law.

**6.4** Unpaid invoices may result in suspension of access until settled.

---

## 7. Messaging, notifications, and automations

**7.1** Laku may send service notifications by in-app notice, email, push notification, SMS, or WhatsApp OTP channels.

**7.2** Campaign “share to WhatsApp” tools may open WhatsApp on your device so you can send a message yourself. That is different from any business API connection.

**7.3** If you enable automations or connect business messaging features when offered, you authorize Laku to process related operational data and to send messages according to rules you configure. You remain responsible for message content, recipient consent, and compliance with Meta/WhatsApp or other provider rules and Applicable Law.

**7.4** Laku is not responsible for third-party messaging outages, template rejections, or account restrictions imposed by Meta or other providers.

---

## 8. Artificial intelligence features

**8.1** Optional AI features (for example Dashboard assistance or automation agent steps) may generate suggestions based on your inputs. Outputs can be incomplete or incorrect.

**8.2** You must review important business actions yourself. Do not use AI to unlawfully extract confidential data or to bypass these Terms or the Privacy Policy.

---

## 9. Third-party integrations

**9.1** Laku may offer optional integrations with third-party systems (for example accounting software). Enabling an integration is your choice and authorization.

**9.2** Third-party terms apply. You must verify critical financial or operational results in the third-party system. Laku does not control those systems.

---

## 10. Acceptable use

You must not:

- violate Applicable Law or third-party rights;
- upload malware or attack the Laku Service;
- impersonate others or submit false business credentials;
- spam, phish, or harass Users;
- interfere with other Users’ use of Laku;
- use Laku to trade prohibited or illegal goods.

We may remove content and suspend Accounts for violations.

---

## 11. Intellectual property

**11.1** Laku and its licensors own the Laku Service, software, brands, and documentation. You receive a limited right to use the Service as permitted under these Terms.

**11.2** You retain ownership of your business content. You grant Laku a license to host and process that content only to operate the Laku Service.

---

## 12. Suspension and termination

**12.1** We may suspend or terminate access for breach, fraud risk, non-payment, legal requirement, or security incidents.

**12.2** You may stop using the Laku Service and request Account closure subject to outstanding fees and legal retention needs.

**12.3** Provisions that by nature should survive (fees, IP, confidentiality, disclaimers, liability limits, governing law) survive termination.

---

## 13. Disclaimers

To the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law, the Laku Service is provided “as is” and “as available.” We do not warrant uninterrupted service or that transactions between Users will meet your expectations. Third-party networks (banks, maps, messaging providers, hosting) may fail outside our control.

---

## 14. Limitation of liability

**14.1** To the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law, Laku is not liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or lost-profit damages.

**14.2** Laku is not liable for disputes solely between buyers and distributors about goods, quality, delivery, or payment, except to the extent caused by Laku’s wilful misconduct.

**14.3** Subject to mandatory law, Laku’s total aggregate liability arising from the Laku Service is limited to the fees you paid to Laku for the Laku Service in the three (3) months before the claim.

---

## 15. Indemnity

You will indemnify Laku against claims arising from your products, content, messaging practices, inaccurate verification data, or breach of these Terms, except to the extent caused by Laku’s wilful misconduct.

---

## 16. Governing law and disputes

These Terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Indonesia. Parties will first attempt good-faith negotiation. If unresolved, disputes shall be brought before the competent courts in **Jakarta, Indonesia**, unless mandatory law requires otherwise.

---

## 17. Changes

We may update these Terms by posting a revised version with a new “Last updated” date. Material changes will be notified through the Laku Service or email where required. Continued use after the effective date constitutes acceptance.

---

## 18. Language

These Terms may be issued in Indonesian and English. If there is a conflict, the **Indonesian** version prevails for use in Indonesia.

---
